words.definition: a large vehicle that carries many people along a fixed route.
words.example: I take the bus to work every day.

words.definition: a vehicle that travels on rails and carries passengers or goods.
words.example: The train arrived on time.

words.definition: an underground train system in a city.
words.example: We took the subway to the museum.

words.definition: a car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.
words.example: We called a taxi to the airport.

words.definition: a building where trains or buses stop for passengers.
words.example: Meet me at the train station.

words.definition: the area at a station where you wait for a train.
words.example: The train left from platform three.

words.definition: the money you pay to travel on a bus, train, or taxi.
words.example: The bus fare is two dollars.

words.definition: a piece of paper that shows you have paid to travel.
words.example: I bought a ticket at the machine.

words.definition: a person who drives a vehicle.
words.example: The bus driver was very friendly.

words.definition: a person traveling in a vehicle but not driving it.
words.example: The bus was full of passengers.

words.definition: a plan that shows the times of buses or trains.
words.example: Check the schedule before you leave.

words.definition: a time when something happens later than planned.
words.example: There was a delay because of the snow.

words.definition: the roads or way you follow to get somewhere.
words.example: This bus route goes through the city center.

words.definition: a place where a bus or train stops for passengers.
words.example: Get off at the next stop.

words.definition: a train or bus that you change to during a journey.
words.example: We missed our connection in London.

words.definition: very full of people.
words.example: The train was crowded during rush hour.

words.definition: the busy time of day when many people travel to or from work.
words.example: Traffic is bad during rush hour.

words.definition: the system of vehicles used to move people or goods.
words.example: Public transport is cheaper than driving.

words.definition: to travel in or on a vehicle.
words.example: I ride the bus to school every morning.

words.definition: to reach a place at the end of a journey.
words.example: The train should arrive at nine o'clock.

text: Every morning, I use public transport to get to work. My house is near a bus stop, so I usually ride the bus to the train station. During rush hour, the streets are busy, and the bus is often crowded with passengers. Sometimes the bus driver has to wait because of traffic, which causes a small delay. At the station, I walk to platform two and wait for my train. I always check the schedule on my phone before I leave home, so I know the exact time. I buy my ticket at a machine, and I pay the fare with my card. My train route goes through three stations before it reaches the city center. Last week, there was a problem, and I missed my connection to the next train. I had to wait twenty minutes for another one, and I arrived at work late! Most days, though, everything works well, and I arrive on time. I like taking the train because it is faster than a taxi and cheaper too. Public transport can be crowded sometimes, but it is still the best way to travel around a big city.
